details: The Federal Reserve maintained interest rates at 3.50%-3.75% for the fifth consecutive meeting on July 29, 2026. However, three out of twelve FOMC members dissented, favoring a 25 basis point rate hike, indicating a "hawkish hold" and persistent concerns about inflation. This decision suggests a less dovish monetary policy path, with potential for further tightening if inflation continues, impacting risk assets like cryptocurrencies. The bond market reacted with the 30-year yield reaching new highs, and the dollar strengthened to a six-month high. Bitcoin saw a modest 1% rise immediately after the announcement, but its August outlook remains closely tied to upcoming inflation and jobs data.
title: Fed Holds Rates at 3.50%-3.75%, Dissent Signals Hawkish Outlook

details: Recent U.S. macroeconomic data shows weaker-than-expected job creation (175,000 vs. 240,000 expected) in the Non-Farm Payrolls report, a slight increase in the unemployment rate to 3.9%, and slowing wage growth. Additionally, the University of Michigan Consumer Sentiment Index came in lower than anticipated. These figures are perceived positively by traditional markets as they increase the likelihood of the Federal Reserve implementing an earlier rate cut, potentially as soon as September. This could stimulate appetite for risk assets, including cryptocurrencies.
title: Weaker US Jobs Data Boosts Hopes for Earlier Fed Rate Cut

details: XRP's price experienced a decline following two key events. New York State filed a lawsuit against prediction market platform Kalshi, alleging illegal gambling operations and seeking substantial damages, which creates significant uncertainty across the prediction market sector. Concurrently, Ripple is scheduled to unlock 1 billion XRP from escrow on August 1st. Although historically only a portion of these tokens enters circulation, this routine unlock represents a consistent source of sell-side pressure on XRP.
title: XRP Slips Amid NY Lawsuit Against Prediction Platform & Token Unlock

details: Russia has announced a ban on cryptocurrency mining in Moscow, Moscow Oblast, and parts of Kursk, effective from August 15, 2026, until December 31, 2032. This regulatory action is expected to impact the global mining landscape and signifies a tightening stance on cryptocurrency-related activities in specific Russian territories.
title: Russia Expands Crypto Mining Ban in Key Regions

details: The market capitalization of U.S. dollar stablecoins has increased by $71 billion (30%) since April 2025, now standing at approximately $308 billion. This growth coincides with the passage of the GENIUS Act in July 2025, which established the first federal regulatory framework for payment stablecoins. This development indicates increasing institutionalization and regulatory clarity within the stablecoin sector, with Tether (USDT) and USDC continuing to dominate over 80% of industry assets.
sourceName: Liberty Street Economics (Federal Reserve Bank of New York)
title: Stablecoin Market Cap Grows Amid New Federal Regulatory Framework
